_about: Planned adventures for the chatroom's 🏚 Adventures tab. Source: docs/sessions/feywild-mansion-plan.md. The GM's truth (§1 of the plan) is deliberately NOT in this file: nothing here is hidden from the model, so nothing here may spoil the twist.

mansions.name: The Feywild House
mansions.premise: Beta Luigi has opened the door of the house in the Feywild. Five areas deep, the party will find keys, ghosts and a crown that should not be where it is.
mansions.scene: A haunted house in the Feywild, entered through the door Beta Luigi opened. Ghosts live in its rooms; most doors are locked and every key opens exactly one. Professor E. Gadd is already inside and acts as the party's guide.
rules: Only the current room exists. Never name, describe or hint at a room the party has not entered.
A locked door stays locked. Nobody opens, breaks or blasts it without the named key, whatever they try.
Keep the marching order exactly as listed. Traps and the first ghost hit the FRONT; ambushes from behind hit the REAR.
Ghosts are played by the narration. Each room's ghosts behave the way the room describes.
What can be found in a room is found only when someone actually searches or fights for it. Describe it plainly and let the party draw the conclusion; never explain what a clue means.
Anyone listed as elsewhere or captured is not in this room and does not speak.

areas.name: Area 4 — the top floor, the roof and the cellars

three_stones.label: 3 Stones
three_stones.effect: Three carved stones that fit something sealed.

shop.name: Gadd's Cart
shop.note: Prices and stock are loose on purpose — Egadd can invent more, at his own prices.

stock.label: Vacuum patch kit
stock.effect: A field repair for a Poltergust.

rooms.name: Foyer
rooms.ghosts: None. Egadd waits here.
rooms.about: A tall double-height hall, dust in the chandelier, a grand stair going up. Egadd's cart of gadgets is parked by the stairs. This is the safe room: nothing attacks here.

rooms.name: Parlor
rooms.ghosts: The Doorman — a stiff, polite ghost who won't let anyone past without a reason.
rooms.about: Velvet chairs, a cold fireplace, a guest book with fresh signatures.

rooms.name: Anteroom
rooms.ghosts: None.
rooms.about: A narrow waiting room with doors off it. One door, to a wardrobe room, will not move at all.

rooms.name: Study
rooms.ghosts: Neville — reads in his chair and hates being interrupted.
rooms.about: Bookshelves to the ceiling, a rocking chair still rocking.

rooms.name: Master Bedroom
rooms.ghosts: Lydia — brushes her hair at the mirror and does not like a draught.
rooms.about: A four-poster bed and a vanity. Curtains stir. A door leads out to a balcony.

rooms.name: Balcony (2F)
rooms.ghosts: None.
rooms.about: Wet stone, Feywild stars, a long drop to the garden.

rooms.name: Nursery
rooms.ghosts: Chauncey — a giant ghost baby who wants to play, and throws a tantrum when he loses.
rooms.about: A rocking horse, a crib, toys that move on their own. This is the first boss.

rooms.name: Washroom
rooms.ghosts: None.
rooms.about: A sink, a towel rack, a key left on the soap dish.

rooms.name: Bathroom
rooms.ghosts: Soapy Sal — a bubbly ghost who hides in the bath foam.
rooms.about: A clawfoot tub full of grey foam.

rooms.name: Ball Room
rooms.ghosts: The Floating Whirlindas — a dancing couple who can only be caught mid-spin — and The Wallflower, who never dances.
rooms.about: A huge dance floor, a dead chandelier, an orchestra pit with no orchestra.

rooms.name: Storage Room
rooms.ghosts: Rattling crates, nothing with a face.
rooms.about: Crates and covered furniture. The back wall sounds hollow; there is a switch behind the crates.

rooms.name: Hidden Room
rooms.ghosts: None.
rooms.about: A dark room behind the wall, a chest on a plinth.

rooms.name: Fortune-Teller's Room
rooms.ghosts: Madame Clairvoya — a fortune teller in a crystal ball. She will read things the party brings her, but she wants proof to read.
rooms.about: Beads, incense, a crystal ball that clouds when anyone lies. She gives the Mirror Room key now and asks them to come back with what they find.

rooms.name: Mirror Room
rooms.ghosts: Vain Vesper — lives in the reflections and only attacks people who look away.
rooms.about: Every wall a mirror. The reflections are a beat late.

rooms.name: Laundry Room
rooms.ghosts: Mrs. Wringer — folds and folds, and wrings anyone who gets in the way.
rooms.about: Washtubs and a mangle. A butler's door at the back, its candles unlit.

rooms.name: Butler's Room
rooms.ghosts: Shivers — the old butler, wandering with a candle. Only shows himself once the candles are lit.
rooms.about: A narrow room, a row of unlit candles, a ring of servants' bells.

rooms.name: Conservatory
rooms.ghosts: Melody Pianissima — plays the piano and asks the party to name the tune.
rooms.about: Glass walls, dead plants, a grand piano that plays itself.

rooms.name: Dining Room
rooms.ghosts: Mr. Luggs — eats without stopping and gets violent when the food runs out.
rooms.about: A long table laid for a feast, plates refilling themselves. A door to the kitchen.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.ghosts: Chef Scorch — a ghost made of stove-fire.
rooms.about: Ovens, hanging pans, a back door to the yard. A cellar hatch in the floor is bolted from below.

rooms.name: Boneyard
rooms.ghosts: Spooky — a ghost guard dog who chases anyone without a reason to be there.
rooms.about: A muddy yard behind a gate that a fire ghost has welded shut; water cools it open.

rooms.name: Graveyard
rooms.ghosts: Bogmire — a ghost of black mud who splits into shadows. Second boss.
rooms.about: Leaning headstones, fog to the knee, one fresh grave.

rooms.name: Billiards Room
rooms.ghosts: Slim Bankshot — a ghost who plays pool with anything round.
rooms.about: Green baize, cues on the wall, balls that roll by themselves. A door into a projection room.

rooms.name: Projection Room
rooms.ghosts: The Usher — shushes, and swells if anyone talks during the film.
rooms.about: Rows of seats, a flickering screen, a reel threaded and waiting.

rooms.name: Courtyard
rooms.ghosts: Gardener Mulch — buries things and doesn't remember where.
rooms.about: A dry fountain, a well, overgrown hedges.

rooms.name: Rec Room
rooms.ghosts: Biff Atlas — a weightlifting ghost who wants a sparring partner.
rooms.about: Punching bags, dumbbells, a mat.

rooms.name: The Twins' Room
rooms.ghosts: Henry and Orville — twin ghost boys who make everyone play hide-and-seek.
rooms.about: Two beds, toy soldiers, a toy box that rattles. The game they start pulls the party apart.

rooms.name: Astral Hall
rooms.ghosts: The Stargazer — a quiet Boo who maps the sky.
rooms.about: A hall painted with constellations that drift. Stairs up to an observatory.

rooms.name: Observatory
rooms.ghosts: None.
rooms.about: A brass telescope and charts pinned everywhere.

rooms.name: Bathroom (2F)
rooms.ghosts: Miss Petunia — bathing, and furious at intruders.
rooms.about: Steam, a shower curtain, a key in the soap.

rooms.name: Washroom (2F)
rooms.ghosts: None — but the Boos like to wait here.
rooms.about: A cracked mirror and a dripping tap.

rooms.name: Nana's Room
rooms.ghosts: Nana — an old ghost knitting, happy to gossip.
rooms.about: A rocking chair, balls of yarn, a cup of tea gone cold.

rooms.name: Tea Room
rooms.ghosts: Earl Grey-Mist — a frosty ghost who insists on manners.
rooms.about: A tea service frozen mid-pour.

rooms.name: Fortune-Teller's Room (return)
rooms.ghosts: Madame Clairvoya, ready to read what they brought.
rooms.about: She reads the film, the twins' riddle and the star chart, and gives a prophecy that only makes sense later.

rooms.name: Safari Room
rooms.ghosts: Big Game Bertram — a hunter ghost who wants a trophy.
rooms.about: Mounted heads that blink, and stairs up to the third-floor balcony.

rooms.name: Balcony (3F)
rooms.ghosts: Boolossus — a giant Boo made of many Boos; freeze it and it bursts apart. Third boss.
rooms.about: A wide stone balcony, wind, the Feywild sky very close.

rooms.name: Cellar
rooms.ghosts: The Coalman — shovels coal into nothing.
rooms.about: Down through the kitchen hatch. Coal, cobwebs, a breaker room door.

rooms.name: Breaker Room
rooms.ghosts: Sparky Phil — an electric ghost who lives in the fuse box.
rooms.about: A wall of switches. Throwing the main breaker puts the whole house in the dark.

rooms.name: Cold Storage
rooms.ghosts: Sir Weston — an ice ghost, a frozen explorer.
rooms.about: Ice on every surface, sides of meat hanging.

rooms.name: Pipe Room
rooms.ghosts: Drip and Drizzle — two ghosts who live in the leaks.
rooms.about: Pipes running up into the dark, toward the top of the house.

rooms.name: Telephone Room
rooms.ghosts: The Operator — connects calls nobody placed.
rooms.about: Dozens of telephones, all ringing.

rooms.name: Armory
rooms.ghosts: The Hollow Guard — empty suits of armour.
rooms.about: Racks of weapons, an old cannon.

rooms.name: Clockwork Room
rooms.ghosts: The Clockwork Soldiers — wind-up toys marching in step.
rooms.about: Gears in the walls, a ticking you feel in your teeth.

rooms.name: Ceramics Studio
rooms.ghosts: Jarvis — a ghost who hides in a pot and plays a guessing game.
rooms.about: Shelves of vases and jars.

rooms.name: Roof
rooms.ghosts: The Weathervane — a spinning ghost who blows people toward the edge.
rooms.about: Slates, chimneys, wind.

rooms.name: Sitting Room
rooms.ghosts: Lady Doily — fussy, and burns hot when her furniture is touched.
rooms.about: Lace and china, nothing out of place.

rooms.name: Guest Room
rooms.ghosts: Sue Pea — sleeps on the ceiling and hates being woken.
rooms.about: The bed is on the ceiling. So is she.

rooms.name: Wardrobe Room
rooms.ghosts: Uncle Grimmly — only appears in the dark, and only to people who look at him.
rooms.about: The door that would not move in Area 1 swings open in the blackout. Wardrobes, mirrors, mothballs.

rooms.name: Sealed Room
rooms.ghosts: Specimen 7 — a lab ghost left behind in a tank.
rooms.about: A door with three stone sockets. Behind it: a laboratory.

rooms.name: The Artist's Studio
rooms.ghosts: Vincent Van Gore — paints ghosts who climb out of their canvases. Fourth boss.
rooms.about: Easels and portraits. Some of the portraits are of people, not ghosts.

rooms.name: Secret Altar
rooms.ghosts: King Boo.
rooms.about: Steps down to a gate, and beyond it an altar lit by painted light.

clues.title: The film reel
clues.found: A home movie: King Boo, gentle for once, teaching a small Boo in a little crown how to haunt.

clues.title: The twins' riddle
clues.found: Henry and Orville say the Prince always won hide-and-seek — "but now he's hiding in a box that hums, and he won't come out."

clues.title: The star chart
clues.found: A chart with one night circled in red ink and a note beside it: the little crown went dark.

clues.title: Nana's gossip
clues.found: Nana, between stitches: royal ectoplasm mends any wound, dearie. Any wound at all. People have come asking.

clues.title: The torn chart
clues.found: A torn page from Dr. Toad's Star Hill Clinic, blown against the railing: Luigi — deteriorating.

clues.title: The calls
clues.found: Every phone replays the same voice, King Boo's, asking one ghost after another: who took my son?

clues.title: The sealed laboratory
clues.found: Extraction notes in a neat old hand, a rack of glass vials with one missing, and a note addressed to "Dr. D."

beats.title: Egadd greets them
beats.text: Professor E. Gadd is waiting just inside the door, thrilled and nervous in equal measure. He greets the party, says he has been studying this house, and offers to guide them. He asks them to decide who goes first and who watches the back.

beats.title: Egadd's vacuum breaks
beats.text: Mid-fight, Egadd's vacuum shrieks, sparks and dies. He insists on fixing it alone and turns his back. Whoever is LAST in the marching order sees into his open bag: a small prince's crown, alone among the tools. Egadd snaps the bag shut and changes the subject.

beats.title: The party splits
beats.text: The twins' game closes doors and drops floors between them. The front of the line and the back of the line are cut off from each other and have to go on alone.

beats.title: Jory is taken
beats.text: Boos pour out of the walls around Jory Dobbs, too many to fight. They drag him into the dark and he is gone. No one can follow.

beats.title: The groups reunite
beats.text: Both halves of the party find their way back to the Fortune-Teller's room and see each other again.

beats.title: Blackout
beats.text: The main breaker goes and the whole house drops into darkness. Somewhere upstairs, a door that would not move clicks open.

beats.title: Mario is already out
beats.text: At the gate of the Secret Altar, Mario is standing there. Not in a painting. Free. King Boo is nowhere to be seen.

beats.title: King Boo attacks
beats.text: After the reunion and a little banter, King Boo rises from the altar, enormous and furious, and attacks. This is the final battle.

beats.title: The paintings release
beats.text: King Boo is beaten. Every painting in the house tears open and the people trapped inside spill out — Jory Dobbs among them.

beats.title: The truth comes out
beats.text: With King Boo beaten, everything they found points the same way: the crown, the humming box, the missing vial, the note to Dr. D. Egadd is confronted. Let him answer in his own words.
